title: Rejecting a plaint at the earliest stage - an underused defence
p1:
Many lawsuits do not fail after a long trial. Some could be stopped before they even begin.

But most people overlook one powerful defence available at the very first stage of a civil case.
p2:
A common misconception is that every plaint (the document through which a civil suit is started) must automatically move forward once filed.

The reality is different. Courts can reject a plaint at the threshold when it does not disclose a valid cause of action, is barred by law, or fails to meet basic legal requirements.

What many litigants miss is that this is not a decision on the entire dispute. It is about asking a simple question: does this case legally deserve to proceed?
p3:
Using this remedy effectively can save years of litigation, unnecessary expenses, and time spent defending claims that should never have entered the courtroom.

A strong defence is not always about winning after the battle begins. Sometimes, it is about showing that the battle should not have started at all.
conclusion: Have you seen cases where an early rejection of a plaint could have prevented years of unnecessary litigation?
